download_figma_images.rationale: The tool fetches image/render data for a Figma file through the authenticated Figma API and returns derived non-public information such as downloaded file paths and image dimensions, so it can expose non-public SaaS data (`SECRET`). It also writes image files under the configured image directory, making it a `WRITE` tool. The returned text can be influenced by Figma image content through dimensions and by Figma/shared design choices used to select images; whether the Figma source is attacker-authored is not fully settled by the code, but arbitrary accessible/shared Figma files are conservatively treated as potentially attacker-controllable (`UNTRUSTED`). The provided source imports but does not include `downloadFigmaImage`, so the exact download implementation is not visible; the surrounding code shows that image URLs from Figma are downloaded and local files are read/overwritten. Local filesystem writes are not treated as `SINK` because they are not attacker-readable under the stated threat model, and the tool does not take an agent-chosen URL/host argument. get_figma_data.rationale: The tool reads Figma file or node data from the fixed Figma API using the user's configured or per-request Figma credentials and returns the serialized design data to the agent, so it can expose non-public SaaS data (`SECRET`). The returned serialized Figma data includes design text, layer/node names, IDs, components, styles, and other content. Whether any particular file is attacker-authored is not fully settled by the code, but because the tool accepts an arbitrary `fileKey`/`nodeId` and returns external Figma document contents, shared/public/multi-writer Figma content is conservatively treated as attacker-controllable (`UNTRUSTED`).
